sections.title: People & Politics
sections.description: Important developments in governments, societies and the people shaping the world.

cards.title: Gaza Ceasefire Fails to Stem Deadly Israeli Attacks, Death Toll Reaches 74,000
cards.content: In Gaza, a 31-year-old mother of five, Fida al-Toutah, was killed in Israeli attacks since the start of the ceasefire on 10 October last year. She is among more than 1,400 people killed in Israeli attacks. Over 300 children have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, including 14-year-old Ismail al-Bardawil, who was shot dead while fishing with his brothers. The ceasefire has not led to significant changes on the ground, with Israeli forces continuing to launch strikes in Gaza almost daily. The total death toll from Israeli attacks since the start of the war in Gaza three years ago now stands at more than 74,000.

cards.title: Zimbabwean Tycoon Wicknell Chivayo Dies in Helicopter Crash
cards.content: Zimbabwean tycoon Wicknell Chivayo, who died in a helicopter crash, was a controversial figure known for his lavish lifestyle, close ties to African presidents, and lucrative government contracts. He was criticized for his lack of transparency and use of black market money. Chivayo was also known for his generosity, giving away cars and cash to influential people, including politicians and musicians. He was a supporter of Zimbabwe's ruling party, Zanu-PF, and had a close relationship with President Emmerson Mnangagwa. Chivayo's death has sparked mixed reactions, with some praising his philanthropy and others criticizing his business practices.

sections.title: Science and technology
sections.description: Discover breakthroughs in science, space, computing and emerging technology.

cards.title: Kagan and Soai Win Nobel Prize in Chemistry for Asymmetry Breakthrough
cards.content: Henri B. Kagan and Kenso Soai have won the 2026 Nobel Prize in chemistry for designing revolutionary experiments that replicated chemical asymmetry, solving a century-old mystery. Their work on chirality, or mirror image forms, allowed them to produce a greater excess of one molecule variant, crucial for pharmaceutical manufacturing. The Nobel committee praised their achievement, saying it provided fundamental new tools and awakened interest in the chemistry of life's origins. The duo shares the 12 million Swedish kronor ($1.2 million) prize, the third award announced this week, following the medicine and physics prizes.

cards.title: Ancient Hunters in Tennessee Valley Carried Tools Based on Local Stone Deposits
cards.content: An analysis of 500 spear points suggests that Ice Age hunters in the Tennessee River Valley decided which tools to carry by knowing local stone deposits. Clovis groups, living there around 13,200 years ago, were more likely to resharpen spearheads, while Cumberland groups, following later, inherited their predecessors' knowledge of chert deposits. This study, published in the Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory, compares tools left behind by these groups to investigate how they adapted to unfamiliar terrain. The findings provide insight into the daily lives and resource management of mobile hunter-gatherers, mirroring modern-day challenges in space exploration.

cards.title: Pioneering Software Engineer Margaret Hamilton Dies at 90
cards.content: Margaret Hamilton, the pioneering software engineer who helped land NASA's Apollo astronauts on the moon, has died at 90. She led a team of 100 engineers at MIT, designing software for NASA's Apollo missions. Hamilton is credited with establishing the field of software engineering and popularizing the term. She received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2016 and the Exceptional Space Act Award in 2003. Her work ensured the success of the Apollo 11 mission, among others, by overriding an errant attempt to swap the flight computer's primary processing. sections.title: Health & wellness
sections.description: Medical research, public health and discoveries that affect everyday wellbeing.

cards.title: Pennsylvania Clinic Sees 1,000 Measles Cases Since April, Urges Vaccination
cards.content: In a measles outbreak in central Pennsylvania, the Central Pennsylvania Clinic is seeing unprecedented cases, with over 1,000 reported since April. The clinic serves vulnerable patients with genetic disorders and has seen a significant increase in hospital admissions and ICU stays. Despite challenges, the clinic has built trust with the Amish and broader Plain community, hosting pop-up vaccination clinics and providing culturally competent care. Vaccination rates are crucial, with the MMR vaccine 97% effective against measles. The clinic's focus is on raising vaccination rates and addressing the community's unique needs, amid the devastating impact of the outbreak.

cards.title: WHO Reports Rare Pneumonic Plague Case at Russian Lab
cards.content: The World Health Organization reported a rare case of pneumonic plague at a Russian institute, causing global concern. A 28-year-old worker died, and hundreds of co-workers were isolated. The WHO Director-General said they have few clear answers about the incident, citing a lack of timely and transparent information sharing. The risk to the general public appears to be low, but the WHO conducts an initial assessment of risk based on an understanding that the Russian lab worker's case could be pneumonic plague, which can spread from person to person.

cards.title: US President Schedules Call with Putin Over Plague Research Death
cards.content: US President Donald Trump says he has a call set up with Vladimir Putin about the death of a lab worker at a plague research centre in Siberia. The worker, 28-year-old Darya Shipilova, died after falling ill a couple of days earlier. Russian officials are investigating the suspected pneumonic plague case, with over 200 people placed under observation. The World Health Organization has called for transparency from Russia, and the US has issued a formal diplomatic message requesting additional information. Mongolia and Lithuania have also taken precautionary measures to prevent potential risks.

sections.title: Environment
sections.description: Climate, oceans, ecosystems and the changing planet around us.

cards.title: WWF Report: Global Wildlife Decline, India Sees Conservation Success
cards.content: The World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF) released its Living Planet Report 2026, which found a 73 per cent decline in the average size of monitored wildlife populations between 1970 and 2022. India, however, recorded gains in the numbers of several major species, including tigers, greater one-horned rhinoceroses, and Asiatic lions. The report highlighted successful conservation efforts in India, but also warned that important challenges remained, including human-wildlife conflict and poaching. The report emphasized the need for a comprehensive approach to conservation, citing habitat loss and degradation as the most frequently reported threats to wildlife populations.

cards.title: Heavy rain and snow hit northern India, with alerts issued for several states.
cards.content: Heavy rain hit Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, while snowfall is expected across higher Himalayan peaks amid strong winds. Heavy rainfall alerts were issued for Kerala, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Sikkim, with thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds posing a threat. In Delhi-NCR, cooler mornings and nights were seen, but daytime temperatures remained high, with isolated thunderstorms and showers possible. Thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds were predicted for Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh, prompting cautionary alerts. The southwest monsoon withdrawal advanced across India, signaling a shift to cooler conditions.

cards.title: India Expects Rain, Snow, Heat, and Thunderstorms
cards.content: Northern hills are expected to experience rain and snowfall, while Delhi and nearby plains face heat and humidity, with temperatures potentially dropping by 2-4 degrees Celsius in the coming days. Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, and Uttarakhand may receive rain, with higher mountain areas potentially witnessing light snowfall. Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram, and Tripura are forecast to receive heavy rain, with a yellow alert issued by the weather department. Several states may also face thunderstorms, lightning, and strong winds, with Pilani recording the country's highest temperature at 40.1 degrees Celsius.

cards.title: Play explores men's mental health through boxing in Belfast
cards.content: A new play, The Corner Man, explores men's mental health through the world of boxing. The story follows Liam Casey, a boxer forced to confront life outside the ring after years of dedication. Writer and producer Cathal J Ferris, who grew up in Belfast, drew inspiration from his own experience of boxing and conversations with fighters. The play highlights the struggle to find purpose and identity after leaving the ring, as well as the importance of talking about mental health. The story is set in Belfast, with the boxing community playing a key role in shaping the narrative.

cards.title: Disney+ to Air 2027 Super Bowl and Monday Night Football
cards.content: >Disney has announced that its streaming service Disney+ will air the 2027 Super Bowl, along with two Monday Night Football games, making it available to all Disney+ subscribers in the US. This is the first time ESPN will produce the Super Bowl, which will also air on ESPN and ABC. The game has already sold out its ad spots, the earliest sellout in Super Bowl history. This move is part of Disney's efforts to expand its live sports streaming offerings, following the launch of a standalone ESPN streaming service and the acquisition of Formula E.

sections.title: economy
sections.description: Markets, businesses, trade and economic changes shaping the global economy.

cards.title: Alberta to Hold Referendum on Independence from Canada
cards.content: Alberta will hold a referendum on October 19, allowing residents to vote on whether to stay in Canada or move forward with a formal binding referendum on independence. Keith Wilson, an Alberta independence supporter, believes the province's unique economy would be richer as an independent country. However, opponents, including Premier Danielle Smith, predict a more sober outcome, citing potential transition costs of C$400bn, lost investments, and trade due to political upheaval. The debate centers on Alberta's wealth, with some arguing it would keep more of its oil and gas revenue, while others warn of the risks and uncertainties of independence.

cards.title: Royal Mail to Cut 2,500 Office Jobs by 2027 for Efficiency Gains
cards.content: Royal Mail plans to cut 2,500 head office and supporting roles by the end of 2027, aiming to improve efficiency and reduce duplication. The 2% workforce reduction will be achieved through voluntary redundancies and employee choices, with frontline postal workers unaffected. The company says the cuts will make it more efficient, but unions argue it's further evidence of a demoralizing and failing institution. Royal Mail has been struggling to meet delivery targets and faces criticism over slow letter deliveries, with an ongoing improvement plan and investments of £500m over five years.

cards.title: Weston Family Buys Boots for $8.9 Billion, Investing in Improved Experience
cards.content: Boots, the UK-based pharmacy and retail chain, has been sold to Canada's Weston family for $8.9 billion. The 177-year-old company, founded by John Boot in 1849, has expanded its business to sell health and beauty products, meal deals, and travel accessories. Despite challenges from rivals and changing shopping habits, Boots has performed well, generating £7.5 billion in sales in its most recent annual results. The Weston family plans to invest in the business, focusing on an improved shopping experience and expansion of healthcare services. The deal is set to be completed in early 2027.
